# A rail reveal slides in but cuts out: dismissal applies display:none at once, so there is no exit motion

Sub-issue of #13158 (dock layouts). Reported by the operator on the Workstation, 2026-09-02 15:35Z: "rails slide in animations are nice now, however, the team forgot about the opposite direction => slide out on focus leave". The entry motion is #18074 / PR #18079, which scoped this out explicitly ("Exit motion — the hidden state is `display: none`; a two-phase hide is its own leaf if wanted"). This is that leaf.

## The Problem

`Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.RevealOverlay#syncSnapshot` adds `neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay-hidden` the moment `visible` turns false, and that class is `display: none` (`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss`). The reveal's content therefore emerges from its strip on entry and vanishes in one frame on dismissal — a dismissal by focus leave, Escape, an outside click, or the pointer leaving after dwell all cut. The asymmetry reads as a glitch next to the entry, and it is the more frequent of the two motions on a rail-heavy layout.

## The Architectural Reality

- `RevealOverlay#syncRevealMotion` opens a `MotionSignal` window on the hidden→visible boundary and closes it on visible→hidden; `onMotionAnimationEnd` closes it on the ROOT's own `animationend` (target identity; the children's ends bubble past). `destroy()` settles without an end event.
- The entry keyframes (`neo-dock-reveal-fade` on the root, `neo-dock-reveal-from-<edge>` on the header and pane slot, `100cqw`/`100cqh` travel against the root's size container) read `--dock-transition-duration-reveal`, which reduced motion collapses to `0ms` at the token layer.
- The iframe shield (`:has(.neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay:not(…-hidden))`) and the rail's outside-pointer listener key on the hidden class and on the machine state respectively.

## The Fix

A two-phase hide, owned by the overlay:

1. On a visible→hidden boundary with a mounted DOM, the overlay stamps `neo-dashboard-dock-reveal-overlay-leaving` instead of `-hidden` and keeps the motion window open. The leaving rules run the reverse of the entry — root fades out, header and slot travel back to the edge — with `animation-fill-mode: forwards`, so the content holds its end state until the hidden class lands one round trip later, and `pointer-events: none`, so the departing panel never takes a click meant for what is under it.
2. On the root's `animationend` while leaving, the overlay applies `-hidden`, drops `-leaving`, and settles the motion window — the same seam the entry already uses. Reduced motion collapses the duration to `0ms`, which still fires the end event.
3. A re-entry while leaving cancels the leave (drop `-leaving`, stay visible); teardown while leaving hides and settles without an end event, as today. A stuck exit (no end event — a consumer sheet that sets `animation: none`) hides after the motion signal's settle grace rather than never.
4. The iframe shield excludes a leaving overlay, so a click into a frame during the exit lands in the frame.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Unit (`DockRevealOverlay.spec.mjs`): a visible→hidden flip on a mounted overlay stamps `-leaving`, not `-hidden`, and keeps the motion window open; the root's `animationend` then stamps `-hidden`, drops `-leaving`, and settles; a hidden→visible flip while leaving cancels the leave; destroy while leaving settles. Red on `dev` for the first.
- [ ] AC-2 Component (`dock-rail-origin` or `dock-rail` fixture): reveal, dismiss with Escape, and the overlay carries `-leaving` with a running animation on its pane slot before it becomes hidden; red on `dev` (hidden lands at once).
- [ ] AC-3 The Workstation's rails, read by eye on the served app: the panel slides back under its strip on focus leave and on Escape, both neo themes.
- [ ] AC-4 The existing reveal, rail, iframe-dismissal and motion-signal suites stay green (`unit/dashboard`, `component/dashboard`).

## Out of Scope

- A reverse slide-in from the current position on a re-entry during a leave. What happens instead, and it is load-bearing: dropping the leaving class changes `animation-name` back, so the browser restarts the ENTRY keyframes from the edge, and that restart's end event is what settles the still-open motion window (corrected after PR #18118's review — the original line claimed a snap-back with no restart).
- Any change to the entry motion or its tokens.

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-09-02T15:36Z: no reveal-exit ticket (#18115 is the native-drop hold, #18074 is the entry, closed by PR #18079); A2A: no claim; Knowledge Base: the motion contract tickets (#13280, #14779, #14780), no leaf.
